title: QBR - NovaEdge Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents in Feb, and roadmap alignment for upcoming product features. Agreed to run a cost-drill, schedule a technical deep dive for latency spikes, and share security/compliance artifacts for upcoming audit.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through NovaEdge's quarterly health check, hope that's still a good agenda?
[00:12] Jordan Patel: Yeah thanks Maya, timing's great. We want to focus on costs and the latency blips we've seen in prod last month.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Perfect, we'll start with usage. Liam, can you pull the usage trend?
[00:27] Liam O'Connor: Sure, uh so in Feb total token usage increased about 42% month-on-month, embeddings up 55% mostly from search feature. The top routes are chat-query and agent-run.
[00:40] Sofia Ruiz: The search embeddings spike aligns with our marketing campaign, we expected more volume but the cost delta was bigger than we planned.
[00:48] Ethan Ward: Yeah finance flagged a 38% increase in spend vs forecast. We're seeing higher per-token costs on the chat route.
[00:56] Maya Chen: Right, a couple things to call out: model choice, dedicated vs hosted routing, and quantization/packaging. We also saw a few long-tail requests that bypassed prefix cache.
[01:08] Priya Kumar: On reliability, there were three short latency incidents last month, two in APAC region during peak hours and one in NA tied to a heavier-than-usual batch job.
[01:20] Jordan Patel: Could you clarify batch job? That was one of our nightly analytics tasks hitting the inference endpoint, yes?
[01:27] Liam O'Connor: Exactly, the scheduled batch wasn't isolated from low-latency routes; it caused KV cache pressure on some dedicated pods. We suggested a routing policy change to isolate heavy jobs.
[01:39] Mina Park: Hmm, if we isolate them to a lower-priority pool what happens to cost?
[01:44] Maya Chen: Usually isolating heavy async workloads to a dedicated cheaper pool lowers tail latency on production routes and can reduce unit-cost if you use quantized model variants for the batch runs.
[01:56] Ethan Ward: Sounds good, can you show the numbers? We need a clear delta for our CFO.
[02:02] Maya Chen: We'll share a cost drill that breaks spend by route/model/region; action item for us.
[02:08] Jordan Patel: Great. On security, our audit is in June — can we get the SOC2 docs and KMS flow for the private deployment?
[02:16] Alex Brooks: Yes we'll send the SOC 2 summary and a diagram of KMS integration. For Private we support bring-your-own-KMS and HSM options.
[02:25] Sofia Ruiz: Also need details on retention and audit logs. Last time logs were sampled, we need full retention policy for 12 months.
[02:33] Priya Kumar: We can share the configuration options and retention tiers; also we have an enterprise export for audit teams.
[02:40] Jordan Patel: Cool. Back to reliability: what immediate mitigations do you recommend for the latency spikes?
[02:47] Liam O'Connor: Short-term: isolate heavy batch jobs to a separate routing tag, enable prefix caching for common prompts, and bump dedicated pool capacity in APAC during campaign windows. Long-term: schedule a kernel/quantization tuning, maybe move some routes to a lower-latency model variant.
[03:03] Mina Park: Are the model variants functionally identical? We worry about quality regressions.
[03:07] Maya Chen: We recommend A/B testing on a small percentage of traffic; Redwood Optimize gives quantization suggestions and quality regressions alarms tied to eval prompt sets.
[03:18] Jordan Patel: Ok. Timeline for the deep technical review?
[03:21] Liam O'Connor: We can schedule a 90-minute deep dive next week to walk through trace logs and run a small benchmark.
[03:28] Sofia Ruiz: Next week works. Prefer Wed or Thu morning PST.
[03:32] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with calendar options.
[03:35] Ethan Ward: On pricing, are there reserved capacity options that could lower per-token cost if we commit?
[03:41] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Dedicated reserved pools give discounts for commits; we can model expected savings based on your forecast. That will be in the cost-drill too.
[03:50] Jordan Patel: Good. Any competitor notes — we're also evaluating Anthropic's endpoint and a heavier on-prem option with Sagemaker.
[03:56] Alex Brooks: Noted, Anthropic and OpenAI were mentioned; we will include comparative notes but focus on latency/cost tradeoffs.
[04:04] Priya Kumar: Action items recap: cost breakdown, SOC2 + KMS docs, schedule deep-dive, run a canary A/B for quantized model.
[04:14] Sofia Ruiz: Also we want a runbook for incident responses and a playbook for scaling during campaigns.
[04:20] Maya Chen: We'll provide a draft runbook and a recommended autoscaling policy with burst options.
[04:27] Jordan Patel: Perfect. Any blockers on data residency? We need EU-only hosting for EU customers.
[04:33] Maya Chen: We support region pinning and VPC options for private; we'll share the config notes.
[04:38] Mina Park: One more thing, roadmap: are there upcoming features for lower-latency streaming or better traceability?
[04:45] Alex Brooks: We're rolling out improved tracing hooks and token-level latency metrics in next quarter, plus streaming enhancements for lower p99.
[04:53] Jordan Patel: That helps our SLO planning.
[04:56] Maya Chen: Great. I'll circulate notes and next steps after this call. Thanks everyone.
[05:02] Jordan Patel: Thanks all.
